rules.rule: Check for known diabetes when fingerprick glucose is low or high
Check for urgent signs when fingerprick glucose is 11.1 or more
rules.problem: Box 2 'Temperature >= 38°C' is missing from the check_for. It is a routine vital, so this is acceptable, but it is the only box item missing. 'Confusion' is encoded with the broader 'Clouded consciousness'.

rules.rule: Check urine for ketones when fingerprick glucose is 11.1 or more
rules.problem: On the page the ketone test follows only when there are no urgent signs ('No: check urine for ketones'). The trigger fires at any glucose >= 11.1. That is conservative, not harmful.

rules.rule: Check for symptoms of diabetes when glucose is 11.1 or more without ketones
rules.problem: Also not gated on the absence of urgent signs, but this matches the No-ketones branch. The footnote-8 symptom list is fully and faithfully covered.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable hypoglycaemia from fingerprick glucose
rules.problem: 'Patient has hypoglycaemia' is stated as fact. Probable is an acceptable encoding. The thresholds <3, or <4 with known diabetes, match.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable diabetes from random glucose 11.1 or more with symptoms
rules.problem: The page says 'Diagnose diabetes', not 'likely', so probable is a reasonable floor. The structure (>=11.1, no ketones, not known diabetes, any footnote-8 symptom) matches the flowchart. The fasting-glucose routes to the same box (FBG >= 7 with symptoms, or repeat FBG >= 7) are not encoded, and neither is 'If < 35 years, type 1 diabetes likely', a probable diagnosis the house standard requires. That is a coverage gap, not invented content.

rules.rule: Urgent: glucose 11.1 or more with danger signs
rules.problem: All 11 box-2 items are present. Box heading 'Check if patient needs urgent attention' supports Urgent. 'Confusion' uses the broader Clouded consciousness. Dehydration lacks the footnote-7 vitals.

rules.rule: Urgent: glucose 11.1 or more with urine ketones
rules.problem: 'Ketones present' leads to box 3, 'Refer urgently', so Urgent is justified.

summary: No invented or wrong content: every condition traces to the page. The most consequential issues are omissions and imprecision. 'Type 1 diabetes likely' (age < 35) and the fasting-glucose routes to 'Diagnose diabetes' are not encoded. 'Confusion' is mapped to the broader 'Clouded consciousness' (closer: 'Confusional state' disorder / 'Acute confusion' finding). The ketone check is not gated on the absence of urgent signs as the flowchart is, and dehydration lacks its footnote-7 vital criteria.
